card: This PR requires that bitcoind's default IPv4 loopback bind succeeds during HTTP server initialization, while keeping the default IPv6 bind optional, and requires all explicitly configured -rpcbind addresses to succeed. If another local process squats on the default IPv4 port, bitcoind previously started on IPv6 and generated an auth cookie, which bitcoin-cli transmitted in plaintext to the squatting process. Commit f103468712 includes a functional test demonstrating local credential exfiltration before the patch. Systems operating in IPv6-only environments will now fail to start under default settings and must explicitly configure -rpcbind.
changed_since_previous: Removed an unused 127.1.1.1 bind option from feature_config_args.py that caused macOS CI to fail under the new fail-closed requirement.
evidence: PR description: "When bitcoind starts and the HTTP IPv4 listen address is occupied by another process, but the IPv6 address is available, the server fails open and generates a cookie file. When bitcoin-cli runs it picks up the cookie file and sends the credentials in plain text to the non-bitcoind process running on the default IPv4 port. An attacker can then use the credentials to commandeer bitcoind over IPv6."
Commit f103468712 adds a regression test demonstrating that a rogue process on 127.0.0.1 captures `bitcoin-cli`'s Authorization header while the node continues listening on IPv6.
problem: When the default IPv4 RPC port is occupied by another local process, bitcoind previously treated the bind failure as non-fatal as long as IPv6 bound. It would write the cookie authentication file to disk, but `bitcoin-cli` defaults to IPv4, transmitting the cookie credentials in plaintext to the foreign process and allowing an unprivileged local user to take control of the node over IPv6.

risk.why: A flaw in bind validation or address resolution could prevent bitcoind from starting or break RPC connectivity, particularly on IPv6-only hosts or unusual network configurations.

summary: Requires the default IPv4 loopback endpoint (127.0.0.1) to bind successfully during HTTP server startup, while leaving the default IPv6 loopback bind optional. In addition, when endpoints are explicitly configured via `-rpcbind`, all must bind successfully or node initialization fails closed. Duplicate bind addresses are also filtered during address parsing.
